gloss: trot; light jog; quick trotting steps

definitions.gloss: trot; light jog; quick short steps
definitions.explanation: Running with short, quick steps — faster than walking but not a full sprint. A light, hurried way of moving, often to catch up with someone or get somewhere quickly without actually running hard.

examples.japanese: {小走|こばし}りで{駅|えき}に{向|む}かった。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{小走|こばし}りで{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}った。
{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}したので、{小走|こばし}りでコンビニまで{走|はし}った。
examples.english: It started raining, so I jogged to the convenience store.

notes:
Describes a pace between walking and running — short, quick steps taken when you need to hurry but aren't sprinting. Very common in everyday narration and descriptions of movement.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {小走|こばし}りで: at a trot, jogging (used adverbially with で)
- {小走|こばし}りに{駆|か}ける: to hurry along at a trot
- {小走|こばし}りになる: to break into a trot

USAGE:
Almost always used with the particle で to describe the manner of movement: {小走|こばし}りで{行|い}く, {小走|こばし}りで{向|む}かう, etc.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {早足|はやあし}: brisk walk, quick pace — fast walking rather than jogging
- {駆|か}け{足|あし}: running, double-time — faster pace, a real run
- ジョギング: jogging — exercise-oriented, not the hurried everyday trot that {小走|こばし}り describes
